correctness.rationale: For each named direction, affine homotheties preserve its equivalence classes. A nontrivial homothety preserves every valuation of cardinality zero, one (when \(q>2\)), or two, so the generated algebra cannot contain all singletons. Conversely, for an arbitrary noncollinear triangle a,a+u,a+v, the intersection of two corresponding modal line-saturations contains exactly the three marked points plus the fourth parallelogram corner. Removing the valuation isolates that corner. Its two modal line-saturations select the other two triangle vertices individually. For any other x, choose two anchor vertices not collinear with x; the intersection of their lines through x is its singleton. The construction uses depth at most three; because the space is finite, all subsets are Boolean unions. In the binary-field case one marker directly defines each other vertex at depth one. An independently implemented finite-field partition refinement and explicit-formula checker passed 11 frame instances, and exhaustive low-support checks passed 832 valuations; these finite checks corroborate but do not prove the general statement. All stated quantifiers, boundary cases \(q=2\) versus \(q>2\), arbitrary dimension \(d\ge2\), and use of named affine directions were examined.

originality.rationale: Targeted searches of published mathematical findings and comparisons with existing mathematical statements did not yield this dimension-independent, every-affine-direction S5 support threshold and depth-three construction. The closest contemporary full source, van Benthem--Bezhanishvili 2022, treats different vector-space modalities (including scalar multiples and addition) rather than individually named parallel-line equivalence operators. Hodkinson--Hussain 2008 studies a two-sorted incidence/parallelism modal logic and non-finite axiomatizability, not the minimum generator of this one-sorted finite powerset modal algebra. Prior finite cyclic three-equivalence grid results overlap for some prime-size two-dimensional instances, but the present claim extends to all dimensions and nonprime fields and proves a constant modal-depth construction that is not implied by the previous claim. These are scientific implication comparisons, not claims of exhaustive global priority. Older affine-geometric logic and other complete sources may contain a latent antecedent.
residual_risks: A pre-2002 or post-2002 affine-geometry modal-algebra paper could phrase the sharp support law implicitly.
The 2002 Balbiani--Goranko paper was available only at abstract level in this review.
Comparison with known related theorems does not establish exhaustive external priority.

value.rationale: The number of marked worlds needed for one-predicate generation is an invariant of a multi-agent finite modal algebra with a geometrically canonical signature: equivalence along every affine direction. The exact dichotomy 1 versus 3 is uniform in arbitrary finite-field order and vector dimension, while the unmarked state set grows as \(q^d\). An explicit finite-depth construction defines every state using at most three modal levels, unlike the logarithmic-depth construction known for the restricted cyclic three-direction case. Every noncollinear triple works and the number of such minimum generators has a closed formula; these give a substantive transparent benchmark for expressivity and state-distinguishability in affine nets. The result is not being presented as a new affine geometry incidence axiom, not a complete census of all generating triples, and not an optimal modal-depth theorem.
